# Coeleo OS — full reference

> Coeleo OS is a from-scratch x86_64 operating system written in Rust: its own kernel, syscall ABI, software compositor, shell and userspace, built in a single repository. It is not a Linux distribution and does not use the Linux kernel.

## Overview

- Target: x86_64, single core, ~512 MiB RAM, software linear framebuffer, no 3D GPU.
- Boot: Limine, on UEFI and legacy BIOS.
- Kernel: one Rust crate, folders by domain, no userspace code linked in.
- Userspace: static no_std ELFs (x86_64-unknown-none) that enter at _start.
- Syscall ABI: 27 syscalls, reached through the libcoeleo wrappers - the only crossing between rings.
- Process model: preemptive round-robin on a 100 Hz LAPIC tick, at most 8 concurrent processes, one thread per process.
- Memory: physical frame bitmap, 4-level paging with strict user/kernel isolation, kernel heap allocator.
- Storage: FAT32 with cluster allocation and long filenames, over VirtIO-blk, SATA AHCI (GPT) or USB Mass Storage.
- Network: smoltcp over virtio-net or Intel e1000e, static IPv4 or DHCP, ARP, ICMP echo, DNS A, HTTP client, TLS 1.2/1.3 via rustls.
- Packages: .coe payloads with Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 integrity verification.
- License: MIT OR Apache-2.0.

## What it is not

- Not a Linux distribution and not Unix-compatible: no libc, no dynamic linking, no POSIX ABI.
- Not derived from Redox, Windows, or an RTOS.
- No SMP, no threads, no Wi-Fi, no audio, no suspend, no 3D acceleration today.

## Build and run

- Host: Linux with QEMU, make, xorriso, python3, mtools and gdisk.
- make all - kernel ISO plus userspace ELFs and test packages.
- make run - UEFI boot with virtio-blk, virtio-net and a USB mouse.
- Other targets: make run-ahci, run-e1000e, run-usb, run-bios, run-hdd.
- Tests run QEMU headless and assert against the serial log.

## Reused components

- Limine - bootloader (UEFI and BIOS).
- Flanterm - terminal emulation.
- smoltcp - TCP/IP stack.
- fatfs - FAT32 filesystem.
- rustls - TLS 1.2/1.3.
- Everything else (memory, scheduler, compositor, syscalls, shell, UI toolkit, installer, package manager) is implemented in the repository.

## Implemented features

### Kernel and hardware

- Boot and CPU foundation: Limine on UEFI and legacy BIOS, GDT, IDT, LAPIC timer and interrupt routing, ACPI and a civil RTC clock. Context switching lives in naked assembly in one file.
- Memory management: A physical frame bitmap (PMM), 4-level paging (VMM) with strict user/kernel address-space isolation, and a kernel heap allocator.
- Preemptive scheduler: Round-robin driven by LAPIC timer interrupts, with a PCB table capped at 8 concurrent processes, zombie reaping and clean resource teardown.
- Syscall layer: 27 syscalls reached through libcoeleo, covering processes, files, pipes, the network, time, window surfaces, system info and the clipboard.
- FAT32 and storage: FAT32 with cluster allocation, long filenames, traversal, read, write, truncate and sync. Disk backends: VirtIO-blk, SATA AHCI with GPT partitions, and USB Mass Storage.
- Networking: smoltcp over virtio-net or Intel e1000e — one PHY, picked at boot. Static IPv4 or DHCP, ARP, ICMP echo, DNS A records, an HTTP client and TLS 1.2/1.3.
- Input drivers: PS/2 keyboard with full scancode translation and key event dispatch; PS/2 and USB HID mice over UHCI and xHCI controllers.

### Desktop

- Software 2D compositor: Pure CPU linear-framebuffer rendering with dirty-rect clipping and selective damage updates, so only what changed is repainted. No hardware acceleration.
- One shared design system: Kernel chrome and Ring 3 applications paint from the same palette and metrics (coeleo-theme), with SDF hairline borders, anti-aliased corners and layered shadows.
- Window management: Floating windows with dragging, 8-direction edge resize, minimise / maximise / close controls, title elision and a glowing accent border on the focused window.
- Panel and launcher: A floating pill or full-width panel with a live clock and network indicator, plus KRunner (Alt+Space) — a modal overlay with fuzzy search and keyboard navigation.
- Graphical file manager: An embedded dual-pane explorer with breadcrumb pills, a Places and Devices sidebar, per-file icons and keyboard navigation.
- Clipboard and notifications: A kernel-level global clipboard behind SYS_CLIPBOARD, shared by the terminal, the shell and GUI apps. Floating rounded toasts report background work, copies and alerts.
- Wallpaper and settings: Full-screen desktop with solid colours or decoded JPEG/PNG wallpapers, with preferences persisted to the disk across reboots.

### Shell and terminal

- Virtual terminal: A Flanterm terminal embedded in the window, with a 16-colour ANSI palette harmonised with the Slate theme, cursor positioning, bold text and clean blits.
- Readline-class shell: Line editing with Home/End, word jumps, kill and transpose; a 128-entry history ring, Ctrl+R reverse search, Tab completion, aliases, semicolons, pipes and redirects.
- Command catalog: 52 builtins across files and directories, text processing (grep, wc, head, tail), processes and memory, storage inspection, packages, networking and power.
- Errors that help: Semantically styled error:, warning:, tip: and usage: prefixes, target-specific descriptions, and a Levenshtein suggestion engine that asks “did you mean…?”.

### Applications and packages

- Signed packages: Ed25519 signatures and SHA-256 integrity verification for .coe payloads, fetched over plaintext HTTP or TLS and installed from disk or the network.
- Text editor: edit, a TUI editor on the virtual terminal, with save and quit shortcuts.
- OS installer: A graphical and CLI installer that deploys the system onto a GPT-partitioned AHCI or USB disk.
- Immediate-mode UI toolkit: libcoeleoui gives Ring 3 apps the same widget language as the desktop; the widgets binary is a live demo of it.

## Kernel domains

- Boot / CPU (boot/): GDT, IDT, LAPIC, console, ACPI, RTC
- Memory (mem/): PMM, VMM, kernel heap
- PCI / USB host (bus/): PCI config space, xHCI
- Disk / FAT (fs/): FAT32, block layer, GPT, AHCI, USB MSC, installer
- Network (net/): smoltcp, HTTP, TLS, DHCP, DNS A, virtio-net or e1000e
- Input (input/): PS/2 keyboard and mouse, UHCI, xHCI HID
- Desktop (ui/): Compositor, panel, KRunner, file manager, VT, windows
- Processes (task/): Preemptive scheduler, syscalls, FDs, pipes, ELF loader

## Userspace applications

- sh: Interactive shell: line editing, completion, dynamic prompt, aliases, builtins
- edit: TUI text editor on the virtual terminal
- widgets: GUI demo of the immediate-mode libcoeleoui toolkit
- install: Graphical and CLI installer for GPT / AHCI disks
- winprobe: Ring 3 surface creation and animation benchmark
- clock: Background graphical clock process
- ls · cat · echo: Standalone command-line file utilities
- hello · fault · spin: Spawn, fault-handling and CPU-loop verification binaries

## Shared libraries

- libcoeleo: Syscall wrappers with an allocation-free, safe API
- libcoeleoui: Immediate-mode UI widget toolkit
- coeleo-theme: Design tokens: palette and layout metrics
- coeleo-draw: 2D primitives: SDF round strokes, text and icons
- coeleo-image: JPEG and PNG decoding for wallpapers
- pkg: Ed25519 verification and .coe package handling

## Roadmap

### Leave the PS/2 desk (Next)

Drivers that stop the machine depending on a 1990s port and a legacy disk controller.

- Phase 27, NVMe: The typical internal SSD is not AHCI. This brings the same FAT tree up on a modern drive.
- Phase 28, USB-Ethernet: Wired networking with no PCI NIC, so a machine with a dongle is not offline.

### Session depth (Then)

What turns a working prompt into a session you can rely on.

- Phase 29, Anonymous mmap and copy IPC: Memory is reached through the library's allocation API today. A general mapping interface is what unlocks the rest of this band.
- Phase 30, Userspace sockets: The TCP/IP stack lives in the kernel today. Sockets expose TCP to Ring 3 without moving where the stack runs.
- Phase 31, HTML subset viewer: Render real documents on the OS itself, starting from a defined subset of HTML and CSS.
- Phase 32, User model: Multi-user sessions and privilege levels, built as a Coeleo-native capability. There are no users or privileges to elevate today.
- Phase 33, NTP: Set the clock from the network instead of trusting the RTC alone.

### CPU, measured first (Later)

One core and a 100 Hz tick already cover the target envelope, so these wait for a measurement that asks for them.

- Phase 34, Tickless LAPIC: Stop paying for a periodic interrupt when nothing is runnable.
- Phase 35, Symmetric multiprocessing: Put every core to work, which means rewriting memory and heap locking end to end.
- Phase 36, Threads inside a process: One thread per process today. Threads need a new PCB, stack and address-space story first.

### Radio, media, laptop (Long term)

Each of these is a project of its own, and each waits on the band above it.

- Phase 37, Wi-Fi: Firmware blobs and 802.11 are where small systems stall, so this lands once wired networking is solid.
- Phase 38, Audio: No sound device is driven today.
- Phase 39, Suspend: S3 sleep states, built on the ACPI work already landed.
- Phase 40, Battery and lid: Power reporting and lid events for laptop use.

### Beyond the reference machine (Vision)

The far horizon: the subsystems that turn a working desktop into a general-purpose platform.

- Phase 41, Compositor and network in Ring 3: Move both out of the kernel, behind inter-process communication.
- Phase 42, Declarative UI toolkit: A higher-level toolkit for building applications, alongside the immediate-mode one.
- Phase 43, Tiling window management: A keyboard-driven tiling layout offered next to the floating desktop.
- Phase 44, EXT4 read and write: A second filesystem, lifting the FAT32 per-file ceiling and adding crash safety.
- Phase 45, POSIX ABI, relibc and shared objects: Dynamic linking and a familiar ABI so software ported from elsewhere can load.
- Phase 46, IPv6: Next-generation addressing alongside the IPv4 stack.
- Phase 47, 3D GPU acceleration: Hardware-accelerated rendering and compute beyond the software framebuffer.
- Phase 48, 5-level paging and IOMMU: A wider address space, plus DMA isolation for device drivers.
- Phase 49, HTML and CSS engine: Extend the same engine toward full document layout and richer web content.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is Coeleo OS?

Coeleo OS is a from-scratch x86_64 operating system written in Rust. It has its own kernel, syscall ABI, software compositor, shell and userspace, all built in a single repository. It is not a Linux distribution and does not use the Linux kernel.

### Is Coeleo OS a Linux distribution?

No. Coeleo OS does not use the Linux kernel and ships no Linux userspace. It reuses a few focused third-party components — Limine for boot, Flanterm for terminal emulation, smoltcp for TCP/IP, fatfs for FAT32 and rustls for TLS — and implements the rest itself.

### Does Coeleo OS run on real hardware?

It boots on UEFI and legacy BIOS machines, and the documented development path is QEMU with virtio-blk, virtio-net and USB input. It targets a single core, roughly 512 MiB of RAM and a software linear framebuffer with no 3D GPU.

### How do I build and run Coeleo OS?

On a Linux host with QEMU installed, run "make all" to build the kernel ISO and the userspace ELFs, then "make run" to boot it under UEFI with virtio-blk, virtio-net and a USB mouse. Targets such as make run-ahci, make run-e1000e, make run-usb and make run-bios cover other disk, network and firmware configurations.

### How is Coeleo OS different from Redox OS?

Redox OS is a Unix-like microkernel system with Linux and BSD source compatibility, POSIX support and a ported compiler toolchain. Coeleo OS is smaller in scope and deliberately not Unix-compatible: the kernel is one crate, there is no libc, no dynamic linking and no POSIX ABI, and programs are static no_std ELFs that enter at _start and talk to the kernel through 27 syscalls. A POSIX ABI, relibc and shared objects are on the long-term roadmap, not implemented today.

### What license is Coeleo OS under?

Coeleo OS is distributed under the terms of either the MIT License or the Apache License 2.0, at your option (MIT OR Apache-2.0). Third-party components such as Limine, Flanterm, smoltcp, fatfs and rustls keep their own licenses.

### Does Coeleo OS support multiple CPU cores?

Not yet. The scheduler runs on one core with a 100 Hz LAPIC tick and a process table capped at eight concurrent processes. Symmetric multiprocessing and threads inside a process are on the roadmap but are not implemented.
